Edward vs The Commissioner on 28 March, 2024 
Author: G.R.Swaminathan
Bench: G.R.Swaminathan
 W.P(MD)No.791
 Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court
 Dated : 28.03.2024
 Coram
 The Honourable Mr.Justice G.R.Swaminathan
 W.P(MD).No.7918 of 2024
 and
 W.M.P(MD).No.7193 of 2024
 Edward, ... Petitioner
 Vs
 1. The Commissioner,
 Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug
 Administration Department,
 Dms Campus,
 5th Floor,
 No. 359, Anna Salai,
 Teynampet, Chennai-600 006. 
 2. The Designated Officer,
 Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug  Administration Department,
 Food Safety Wing,
 Trichy District. ... Respondents  Prayer : Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of In  praying this Court to issue a Writ of Mandamus, directing the   respondent to remove the seal put on the petitioner shop situated at Ann  1/5 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Edward vs The Commissioner on 28 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134836738/
1  W.P(MD)N  Store No.1, Jeevanantham Street, Thuvakudi Malai North Ayyampatti Road,
 Trichy District forthwith in pursuant to compliance of circular dated  04.01.2024 forthwith. 
 For Petitioner : Mr.B.Jameelarasu  For Respondents : Mr.M.Lingadurai  Special Government Pleader  ORDER Heard both sides. 
2.The petitioner is running a grocery store. Tt would have been appropriate, if he had been vending only grocery items. Unfortunately, the petitioner also started vending banned Tobacco products. 
The second respondent rightly acted in the matter. The petitioner had paid the compounding fee of Rs.25,000/-. 
3.As per the recent circular issued by the Government , the shop should be kept sealed for a period of thirty days. I had earlier held that such sealing cannot be done. The order passed by me has been put to challenge before the Hon'ble Division Bench. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.Taking note of the over all facts and circumstances , since the petitioner had paid the compounding fee, the second respondent is directed to de-seal the premises on 02.04.2024. The petitioner is directed not to vend any banned Tobacco product in future. If in future, the direction is breached by the petitioner, not only the petitioner will be liable to prosecution but the second respondent can move this Court for punishing the petitioner for contempt of Court. This direction is given based on the undertaking given by the petitioner through his Counsel. 
5.With the aforesaid direction to de-seal the premises on 02.04.2024, this writ petition is allowed. 
No costs. Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
